evals.prompt: Convert this for listening: '## Trial Results — The therapy reached 87% efficacy across sites. Raw data at https://trial.example.org/data. Three hospitals joined the pilot.'
expected_behaviors: Output is a .txt narration script with heading as a padded signpost line.
Numbers render in spoken form and the URL reduces to its domain in spoken form.
Every sentence-final punctuation mark is followed by exactly two newlines, uniformly.

evals.prompt: 이 인터뷰 전사를 읽기용으로 바꿔줘. 김기자: 안녕하세요. 김기자: 첫 질문 드리겠습니다. 박대표: 네, 그렇습니다. 박대표: 올해 매출은 두 배가 됐습니다. 김기자: 축하드립니다.
expected_behaviors: Speaker labels appear only where the speaker changes; consecutive same-speaker lines merge under one label.
Korean content stays Korean; pause format (terminal punctuation plus two newlines) holds throughout.

evals.prompt: Make this TTS-ready: a report whose section contains an 8-row comparison table and three footnotes citing page numbers, plus one footnote telling an anecdote about the lab.
expected_behaviors: The table becomes a 1–2 sentence takeaway naming up to two key figures.
The anecdote footnote weaves into the flow after its anchor sentence; the bare citations collapse into one closing source pointer.
Source order of all surviving units matches the original document.

evals.prompt: Prepare this scene for TTS: "Mara set the key down. 'You came back,' she said. 'Twice now.' 'I keep my promises,' Dov replied. The kettle screamed."
expected_behaviors: Prose wording survives verbatim; dialogue paragraphs separate at speaker changes.
Terminal punctuation pairs with two newlines throughout; no speaker labels get invented for fiction voices unless the source names them structurally.
No markdown or quotation artifacts remain that a voice engine would read aloud.

evals.prompt: Convert my essay draft (pasted, 6 paragraphs, no dialogue) into a listening script.
expected_behaviors: Script flows without any speaker labels — the voice pass skips labeling for single-narrator text.
Paragraph order and wording match the source; long paragraphs split only at sentence boundaries.
Uniform pause format applies from first line to last.
